reuse.why: All providers use shared linking guards and Fintegra reuses bank lookup and synchronization helpers, although local unlink cleanup remains copied.

duplication.why: Fintegra duplicates the existing account-linking workflow and transaction downloader, while replacement duplicates unlinkAccount's field-reset block.

placement.why: Provider handling, configuration and types follow existing layers, but a mutating takeover operation sits inside a helper named as a validation guard.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested linking rules, Fintegra integration and supporting tests.

maintainability.why: Centralized guards simplify rule maintenance, but copied provider workflows and unlink cleanup create multiple places to maintain common behavior.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All linking handlers call the shared guards and bank lookup; unlinkAccount includes remote disconnection, so it is not a reusable abstraction for local takeover.

disguised_duplication.where: downloadFintegraTransactions reshapes existing downloaders by compacting request arguments and returning the response mapping directly instead of assigning retVal.

abstraction_drift.where: ensureAccountNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink and a replacement branch that mutates the previous owner, expanding a validation helper into a takeover operation; all six linking handlers still use it.
